rubrics.justification: Accurately interprets morphology from the provided Gardner/lab description, correctly describing B-grade ICM and TE and noting the expansion-stage labeling nuance; appropriately avoids fabricating image-only features since no image was provided.
Thoroughly integrates age, tubal factor diagnosis, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, endometrium, lifestyle, prior cycle history, and semen parameters with embryo quality to contextualize prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with the prognosis estimate clearly tied to fair embryo morphology moderated by strong patient-level favorable factors and relevant caveats.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice standards, including SET, attention to hydrosalpinx, and cautious use of PGT-A in a young first-cycle patient; minor uncertainty remains around exact implantation percentages and grading nomenclature nuance.
Provides practical next steps for the current transfer and sensible future planning, including hydrosalpinx assessment, luteal/timing optimization, and when to escalate evaluation after failure.
